description_en: A stone pavilion from approx. 14th-15th century.The pavilion is located on the western terrace of the Jagannātha temple complex, 1,5 kilometres south-east from Chipur.The monument is built on a square stone platform. Eight pillars support the corbelled dome of the pavilion. There are three pillars on each side of the pavilion. Each pillar is carved on its four sides with various motifs in bas-relief: warriors, horse riders, geometric patterns, etc. The pillars support an entablement made of large stone beams, one on each side.The pavilion is very similar in style and dimensions to the "Royal Pavilion" in Ajayamerukoṭa (DDL0140). Given the historical context of the area and the monument's features, it is possible to date it from approximately 14th-15th century.The pavilion was briefly described by D. R. Sharma (Sharma 2012, p. 292-293).
references: REFERENCES Sharma, Dilli Raj. 2012. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies.
